title: Venous Thromboembolism in Pregnancy and Postpartum

evidenceAudit.scope: Pregnant and postpartum women: VTE risk assessment and thromboprophylaxis, diagnosis of suspected DVT/PE, and treatment around labour and breastfeeding. Verified against the Saudi MOH VTE prophylaxis protocol (RCOG-based obstetric tool), MOH DVT (2024) and PE (2022) protocols and the ESC/ERS 2019 PE guideline summary; contraindications from FDA labels. pathophysiology.summary: Pregnancy is a hypercoagulable state (Virchow's triad): raised clotting factors and fibrinogen, reduced protein S and fibrinolysis, venous stasis from progesterone and uterine compression of the iliac veins, and vessel injury at delivery. Risk is highest postpartum, especially after caesarean birth.
keyMechanisms: Hypercoagulability is physiological preparation for blood loss at birth and persists for about 6 weeks postpartum.
Left iliac vein compression explains the predominance of left-sided and iliofemoral DVT in pregnancy.
Added risks: previous VTE, thrombophilia, obesity, age over 35, parity 3 or more, caesarean section, PPH, pre-eclampsia, infection, immobility, IVF/OHSS, hyperemesis (MOH/RCOG tool).
D-dimer rises through pregnancy — above 500 µg/L in up to 25% in the third trimester — so it cannot be used alone (ESC).
Warfarin crosses the placenta (teratogenic, fetal bleeding); heparins do not — LMWH is the anticoagulant of choice.

symptoms: DVT: unilateral leg pain and swelling (usually left), especially of the calf or whole leg.
PE: breathlessness, pleuritic chest pain, haemoptysis, syncope — overlap with normal pregnancy symptoms.
physicalSigns: Leg swelling (calf circumference difference), tenderness, warmth.
Tachycardia, tachypnoea, hypoxaemia; hypotension in massive PE.
redFlags: Haemodynamic instability (massive PE) — manage with the same emergency algorithm as non-pregnant patients
Recent (within 1 month) acute VTE near term — plan IV UFH around delivery
precipitants: Caesarean section (especially in labour), PPH above 1 L, preterm birth, stillbirth.
Obesity, age over 35, parity 3+, smoking, immobility, dehydration, infection.

clinicalManagement.title: Assess risk at every stage
actions: Score with the MOH/RCOG obstetric tool; reassess on admission and after delivery.
Low risk: mobilise, avoid dehydration. Intermediate/high risk: LMWH plus mechanical methods.
Avoid or delay pharmacological prophylaxis in women at risk of bleeding after weighing risks.

clinicalManagement.title: Thromboprophylaxis
actions: Enoxaparin once daily by weight: below 50 kg 20 mg; 50–90 kg 40 mg; 91–130 kg 60 mg; 131–170 kg 80 mg; above 170 kg 0.6 mg/kg/day (MOH). UFH 5000 units SC twice daily is the alternative.
Antenatal: high risk from first trimester; intermediate from 28 weeks. Postnatal: at least 10 days; 6 weeks if on antenatal LMWH.

clinicalManagement.title: Suspected DVT or PE
actions: Start treatment-dose LMWH while awaiting imaging unless contraindicated (stabilise and anticoagulate before confirmation — MOH PE approach).
Use a formal pregnancy diagnostic pathway: clinical probability, D-dimer within the algorithm, leg compression ultrasound, then CTPA or V/Q scan.
Unstable PE: same emergency algorithm as non-pregnant (oxygen to SpO2 90% or more, consider reperfusion).

clinicalManagement.title: Treatment of confirmed VTE
clinicalManagement.timeframe: Throughout pregnancy and at least 6 weeks postpartum
actions: LMWH (prefilled single-dose syringes — multi-dose vials contain preservatives and are contraindicated): enoxaparin 1 mg/kg every 12 h (MOH).
CrCl below 30 mL/min: UFH (IV 80 units/kg bolus then 18 units/kg/h, or SC) instead of LMWH.
No warfarin in pregnancy (teratogenic); no rivaroxaban or apixaban in pregnancy or breastfeeding. Fondaparinux if heparin-induced thrombocytopenia.

clinicalManagement.title: Labour and birth
actions: Stop LMWH at least 24 h before planned delivery; no neuraxial anaesthesia if fully anticoagulated when labour starts.
VTE within the last month: switch to IV UFH (stop 4–6 h before delivery). Preterm delivery risk: switch to IV UFH at 36 weeks (MOH).
Restart LMWH 6 h after vaginal birth or 12 h after caesarean if no significant bleeding.
Postpartum: LMWH or warfarin (both safe with breastfeeding).

learningObjectives: Assess VTE risk in pregnancy and the puerperium, give weight-based thromboprophylaxis, and diagnose and treat DVT/PE safely around birth.
pitfalls: Using D-dimer alone to exclude VTE in pregnancy.
Withholding CTPA/V/Q out of radiation concern when PE is suspected.
Neuraxial anaesthesia within the LMWH window.
Forgetting postnatal prophylaxis after caesarean birth.
keyPoints: Score VTE risk at booking, admission and after birth.
Enoxaparin prophylaxis by weight band; 10 days or 6 weeks postnatally.
Treat with enoxaparin 1 mg/kg twice daily; start before imaging.
No warfarin or DOACs in pregnancy.
Stop LMWH 24 h before planned birth; restart 6 h (vaginal) or 12 h (caesarean).
